record.paper_title: Polycyclic Codes Associated with Trinomials: Good Codes and Open Questions
record.original_question: Do there exist any binary polycyclic codes that are self-dual, self-orthogonal, or dual-containing, or are all three phenomena impossible over the field F_2?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.10. There is no self-dual or self-orthogonal or dual-containing polycyclic codes over the binary field.

artifact.status_search_result: Web searches turned up extensive related work on polycyclic codes (annihilator-duality, skew polycyclic codes, polycyclic codes over serial rings, double polycirculant constructions from trinomials), but no source explicitly confirming or refuting the conjecture that no binary polycyclic code can be self-dual, self-orthogonal, or dual-containing. The status is therefore not clearly established by the available sources.

status_evidence.title: Polycyclic codes over serial rings and their annihilator CSS construction
status_evidence.snippet: Necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of annihilator self-dual, self-orthogonal, LCD, and dual-containing polycyclic codes over a class of serial rings.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses self-dual/self-orthogonal/dual-containing polycyclic codes via the annihilator inner product, not the Euclidean one over F_2.

status_evidence.title: On the duality and the direction of polycyclic codes
status_evidence.snippet: Studies duality structure of polycyclic codes.
status_evidence.claim: General duality theory of polycyclic codes is developed, but the specific binary Euclidean conjecture is not resolved here.
